outcome: Hector Pasten's September 2026 preprint unconditionally improves the best known bound on the quantity Szpiro's conjecture is about — from log|Δ| ≪ N log N (2013) to log|Δ| ≪ N log log N in general, and to log|Δ| ≪ N for semistable curves — but the conjecture (log|Δ| ≪ (6+ε)log N, i.e. |Δ| ≤ C(ε)·N^(6+ε)) remains open.
summary: The only substantive event in the window is Hector Pasten's solo-authored arXiv preprint 'Improved bounds for Szpiro's conjecture' (arXiv:2609.17390), submitted 2026-09-15, with a single version (no revision history yet). It builds on Pasten's own prior work approaching the abc conjecture via Shimura curves and unconditionally proves log|Δ| ≪ N log log N for all elliptic curves over Q (previously this strength was known only conditionally, under GRH; the best prior unconditional bound, from 2013, was the weaker log|Δ| ≪ N log N), and log|Δ| ≪ N in the semistable case. This is a genuine improvement to the bound at the heart of the conjecture (which asks for log|Δ| ≪ (6+ε)log N), so it is scope-relevant under §3.1 — the record of best known bound is exactly what the bullet's inequality concerns. However, the conjecture itself is nowhere near settled (log N vs N log log N is an enormous gap), so this is `progress`, not `partial` or `resolved`: no case or restriction of the full statement has been proved, only the auxiliary quantity has moved, matching the guidance that a bound moving on a still-open problem is `progress`/`ai_role` `bound` territory (moot here since no AI was involved). The preprint is only about a week old with no journal acceptance, no digestion by Tao or another expert found (searched Tao's blog, Mathstodon, general web), and a 'pith.science' page that summarizes the paper appears to be an automated/AI paper-summary aggregator rather than expert review, so it does not count as digestion. I found no mention of any AI system, LLM, or automated theorem prover in the abstract/paper (via WebFetch of the abs page; the PDF text extraction itself failed, returning binary stream data, but the abstract-page summary and lack of any acknowledgements-style claim gives no indication of AI use) — this is standard solo human number-theory work. Separately, a Zenodo item, 'A Spectral Proof of Szpiro's Conjecture via K-Theoretic Determinants: Complete Conductor Revolution' (Sept 2025) by Luis Morató de Dalmaes / Luis Morató de Dalmases, claims a full proof via a 'CronNet-Holo framework' and explicitly invokes AI/ML-flavored terminology ('CronNet'). Investigating this author further, they have self-published dozens of similarly-named 'CronNet-Holo' items on Zenodo since May 2025 spanning unrelated topics (Riemann Hypothesis, cosmology, quantum materials, even crop circles), a pattern strongly indicative of a crank/fringe author (possibly using an AI system to generate volumes of pseudo-mathematical text), not a credible mathematical result. No institutional affiliation, no peer review, and content spanning implausibly disparate fields for one 'unified framework' — this is excluded from the numerator per the instructions to only count credible, expert-reviewable work; it is not evidence of a genuine result, AI-produced or otherwise, and I do not classify it as an AI-involved mathematical advance because there was no real mathematical content to attribute. Net: one real advance (Pasten, no AI), one fringe non-event (Zenodo, excluded). Status is `progress`, ai_role `none`.
competing_reading: One could argue the Zenodo item still deserves an `incident` classification if it were treated as 'an AI-produced claim that was announced ... then withdrawn' — but it was never picked up by anyone as a serious claim to begin with (no coverage, no discussion, self-published on a preprint repository with no gatekeeping), so it never rose to the level of an 'announced' claim that needed withdrawing; treating it as a real incident would overstate its significance. I classified it as not worth recording as an event at all, which is the more conservative reading.
what_would_settle_it: Whether the mathematical community (via a citation, a follow-up paper, or a blog digestion) treats Pasten's bound as correct and significant would move it toward wider recognition, but would not change its `progress` status since the conjecture itself is not closer to resolved in kind, only in degree. For the conjecture itself, only a proof of log|Δ| ≪ (6+ε)log N (or a genuine counterexample) would change the status to resolved/claimed.

events.credibility_reason: Landmark problem (equivalent in strength to a form of abc) claimed in an ungated repository; author has self-published dozens of 'CronNet-Holo' items across unrelated fields (Riemann Hypothesis, cosmology, crop circles); no affiliation, no uptake; the September 2026 Pasten paper on the same quantity treats the conjecture as open.

judgement.doubts: The semistable result log|Δ| ≪ N is still a bound on a class, not the conjectured (6+ε)log N inequality for that class, so it is not a case settlement. The Pasten PDF full text was not readable; absence of AI disclosure is inferred from the abstract page only.
